key_insight: Critical-State RL finds the specific turns in a multi-turn tool-use trajectory that are actually trainable, instead of treating all reward variation as equally informative. It separates real action effects from downstream randomness so learning focuses on the calls that matter.
problem_solved: Multi-turn tool-use systems can fail because of a single important model call, but standard reward signals often cannot tell which call caused the outcome. This paper addresses the challenge of diagnosing which intermediate states deserve credit assignment and training when later interactions introduce noise.
method: Identify task-defined candidate calls within a multi-turn interaction.
Use local rewards to test whether reward variation reflects the current action's effect rather than downstream stochasticity.
Classify states as trainable when their reward signal is sufficiently diagnostic, enabling targeted reinforcement learning updates.
impact: This helps practitioners focus training on the truly critical decisions in tool-using agents, improving sample efficiency and reducing wasted optimization on noisy states. It is especially useful for debugging and improving long-horizon agent behavior in complex workflows.
visual_elements: A multi-turn conversation timeline highlighting candidate tool calls and the single critical state
A causal diagram showing current action effects versus downstream randomness
A reward signal plot comparing informative and noisy states
An icon-based flowchart from state diagnosis to targeted RL training
paper_title: Critical-State RL: Diagnosing Trainable States for Multi-Turn Tool Use
paper_authors: Zixiang Chen, Wenting Zhao, Zhepeng Cen, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu
